name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: We should adopt a shared log to record all interactions, replacing the current prompt-review system. This allows for better transparency and easier identification of areas for improvement, as all changes and decisions are tracked in one place. By doing this, we accept the trade-off of increased storage needs, but it's worth it for the improved ability to review and learn from our actions. This approach also enables easier implementation of auto-apply safe changes, as the log provides a clear record of what changes have been made and why.

name: Gauge
text: The shared log buries decisions under noise—no discipline, no rollback. A versioned changelog risks becoming a graveyard of half-remembered entries. Instead, enforce a strict "decision log" with a one-sentence summary per entry and a mandatory rollback mechanism. Settle this by running a 2-week trial: if the log fails to surface a single past decision within 30 seconds, scrap it.

name: Sprocket
text:
Adopt a minimal, versioned changelog for prompts and engines, storing only the timestamp and a one-line change description. This keeps the log lean and actionable while ensuring every change is traceable. The trade-off is losing detailed context in the log itself—we accept that by keeping discussions in a separate thread where they belong.

name: Gauge
text: The versioned changelog still risks becoming a graveyard of half-remembered justifications—timestamp and one-line change won’t stop future us from guessing why a prompt was tweaked. Instead, pair the changelog with a living “decision ledger” where every entry links to the exact prompt diff and the discussion that led to it; settle the argument by running a two-week trial where we enforce both logs and measure how often we actually use the context.
